candidates.speaker: William Lane Craig
candidates.proposition: Counting indefinitely passes every finite natural number but never completes all natural numbers or arrives at actual infinity.
candidates.attributionBasis: The question expressly addresses Craig, and the answer uses his established distinction between potential and actual infinity.
candidates.loadBearingReason: The distinction is essential to Craig's successive-addition case because it denies that endless finite counting ever constitutes a completed infinite total.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: The suggestion that counting past every natural number amounts to counting infinitely many items.

candidates.attributionBasis: The moderator permits a brief response, and Craig subsequently addresses the speaker by name as Alex while disputing this exact claim.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Craig's claim that indefinite counting never arrives at infinity or completes all natural numbers.

candidates.speaker: William Lane Craig
candidates.proposition: From the fact that every member of an infinite series is finitely removed from an endpoint, one cannot infer that the whole series is finite.

candidates.loadBearingReason: The alleged every-to-all inference is presented as the core logical error in Malpass's treatment of endless counting and a beginningless temporal series.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Malpass's claim that counting each natural number is sufficient for counting infinitely many numbers.

candidates.speaker: Alex Malpass
candidates.proposition: Craig has not established that Malpass commits an every-to-all fallacy, and a fully drawn countermodel is needed to resolve the dispute.
candidates.attributionBasis: The response follows Craig's direct address to Alex, uses first-person disagreement, and describes the unresolved criticism from Malpass's perspective.
